title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Termly Exam #6 (Term 3)

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a good way to pray? (1 mark)
   A. Shout
   B. Ask only for gifts
   C. Say thank you and ask for wisdom and kindness
   D. Sit and laugh

2. According to the teaching, what happens to good actions? (1 mark)
   A. They are forgotten
   B. They bring bad luck
   C. They have no results
   D. They bring good results

3. Which king protected a dove in a well-known story? (1 mark)
   A. Harishchandra
   B. King Shibi
   C. Hiranyakashipu
   D. Ravan

4. Because God sees all we do, what should we do? (1 mark)
   A. Be honest even when alone
   B. Hide
   C. Cheat
   D. Complain

5. What does Artha mean? (1 mark)
   A. Prayer
   B. Honest wealth and the things we need
   C. War
   D. A river

6. Which important idea about the Purusharthas is taught? (1 mark)
   A. Wishes come first
   B. Ignore Dharma
   C. Balance, with wealth and wishes following Dharma
   D. Wealth is all that matters

7. What does the Shibi story teach? (1 mark)
   A. A kind person protects the weak
   B. Hawks always win
   C. Doves are bad
   D. Kings do not care

8. What does Prarthana mean? (1 mark)
   A. Prayer
   B. Duty
   C. Wealth
   D. Rebirth

9. Which of the five principles is about being born again? (1 mark)
   A. Prani Daya
   B. Purushartha
   C. Prarthana
   D. Punarjanam

10. How long is Paryushan in one Jain tradition? (1 mark)
   A. Eight days
   B. One month
   C. One year
   D. Two days

11. Why do the dates of Maha Shivratri and Paryushan change on the usual calendar? (1 mark)
   A. They follow the school terms
   B. They follow the market days
   C. They follow the shops
   D. They follow the Moon

12. What do Jains say on the last day of Paryushan? (1 mark)
   A. Om Namah Shivaya
   B. Sat Sri Akal
   C. Micchami Dukkadam
   D. Namaste

13. Which Jain scripture is often read during Paryushan? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Granth Sahib
   B. Dhammapada
   C. Kalpasutra
   D. Ramayan

14. What does fasting on Maha Shivratri show? (1 mark)
   A. Laziness
   B. Self-control
   C. Greed
   D. Anger

15. In which months does Paryushan usually occur? (1 mark)
   A. August or September
   B. February or March
   C. December
   D. June

16. What is the Indian name for Sunday? (1 mark)
   A. Ravivaar
   B. Shanivaar
   C. Somvaar
   D. Mangalvaar

17. What does vaar mean? (1 mark)
   A. Year
   B. Day of the week
   C. Month
   D. Planet

18. What is the Indian name for Wednesday? (1 mark)
   A. Shanivaar
   B. Somvaar
   C. Guruvaar
   D. Budhvaar

19. What is the Indian name for Monday? (1 mark)
   A. Ravivaar
   B. Budhvaar
   C. Guruvaar
   D. Somvaar

20. Ravi is another name for which heavenly body? (1 mark)
   A. Mars
   B. The Sun
   C. Venus
   D. The Moon

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain the four Purusharthas with one example each for a child. (4 marks)

22. Explain the words Micchami Dukkadam said at Paryushan. (2 marks)

23. State three ways of showing respect to the National flag and Anthem. (3 marks)

24. What does Prani Daya mean? (2 marks)

25. Draw a timeline from January to December and mark Maha Shivratri, Madaraka Day and Paryushan. (4 marks)

26. What is a rite or ritual? Give one example. (2 marks)

27. Describe how a child can follow all five principles in one day. (5 marks)

28. Which festival in the lesson is a national holiday and why? (2 marks)

29. Explain the importance of celebrating Madaraka Day. (3 marks)

30. Describe how Paryushan Parva is celebrated. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Say thank you and ask for wisdom and kindness
   Ask for wisdom, not only gifts.

2. D — They bring good results
   Good actions bring good results.

3. B — King Shibi
   King Shibi saved the dove.

4. A — Be honest even when alone
   Honesty at all times.

5. B — Honest wealth and the things we need
   Artha is earning in an honest way.

6. C — Balance, with wealth and wishes following Dharma
   Dharma guides the others.

7. A — A kind person protects the weak
   Kindness protects the weak.

8. A — Prayer
   Prarthana is prayer.

9. D — Punarjanam
   Rebirth.

10. A — Eight days
   Eight days in one tradition and ten in another.

11. D — They follow the Moon
   The Indian calendar is based on the Moon.

12. C — Micchami Dukkadam
   It asks for forgiveness.

13. C — Kalpasutra
   Many Jains hear the Kalpasutra.

14. B — Self-control
   It teaches self-control.

15. A — August or September
   It falls in Bhadrapada.

16. A — Ravivaar
   Ravi is the Sun.

17. B — Day of the week
   Vaar means day.

18. D — Budhvaar
   Budh is Mercury.

19. D — Somvaar
   Som is the Moon.

20. B — The Sun
   Ravi is the Sun.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Dharma: doing homework and telling the truth. Artha: saving pocket money honestly. Kama: enjoying play and friendship. Moksha: praying and growing kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: May any harm I did in thought, word or deed be forgiven.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for forgiveness.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stand straight, be quiet, never let the flag touch the ground, learn and sing the anthem (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Kindness to all living beings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for kindness and living beings.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: A line from January to December with Maha Shivratri in February or March, Madaraka Day on 1 June and Paryushan in August or September.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the line and months, 1 mark for each correct festival.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: A special action done in a set way at a festival, such as lighting a lamp or raising a flag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Morning prayer and Namaste (Prarthana, Paramatma), honest schoolwork (Dharma, Artha), helping a friend (Prani Daya), thinking about the day's good deeds (Punarjanam and karma).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each principle applied, up to 5.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Madaraka Day, because it marks a step in Kenya's history and all Kenyans celebrate it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: It reminds us of Kenya's step to self-government on 1 June 1963, teaches patriotism and unity, and lets us respect the flag and the anthem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: Jains fast, pray and meditate, listen to scriptures such as the Kalpasutra, practise Ahimsa, give to the needy and ask for forgiveness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct practice, up to 3.
